speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing issues with your gait and coordination. Could you please tell me when these symptoms started and if they have been getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The asymmetry of your symptoms, specifically the clumsiness on the right side, is a crucial detail that suggests a focal neurological issue rather than a systemic one. Have you experienced any headaches, double vision, difficulty speaking, or loss of sensation in your face or limbs alongside these coordination problems?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The use of natalizumab for Crohn's disease significantly raises the suspicion for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), which often presents with focal neurological deficits like those you described. Have you experienced any changes in your vision, such as blurriness or loss of peripheral vision, or any subtle changes in your memory or personality?

text:
The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement are classic for PML, even with a negative JC virus index, which can occur in early stages or due to assay limitations. Given your history of natalizumab use and these specific imaging results, the clinical picture is highly consistent with this diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
